summary: A humorous local-interest piece on the adoption of electric and autonomous vehicles in the writer's community. It covers the mayor's announcement of an all-electric plan, myths about EVs and self-driving cars, teething troubles, a community education fair, environmental benefits, and worries from taxi drivers. The tone is light, but it concludes that the technology promises a cleaner, more efficient future.
one_line: A comic local feature on a community's shift to electric and autonomous vehicles, covering the mayor's pledge, myths, a public fair, and job worries.
key_facts: On September 12, 2023, Mayor Bob "Bolt" Johnson announced the city's plan to go electric, saying "No more gas guzzlers! We go electric!"
The crowd applauded the mayor's speech, though half seemed to be clapping for the end of the speech rather than its content.
The article debunks the myth that EVs are powered by lightning captured during storms; they simply run on electricity.
A common myth holds that EVs cannot be driven beyond sight of home without needing a plug, but modern EVs go many miles.
The article says autonomous cars are run by sensors and algorithms, not by a mini spirit or genie inside the vehicle.
Harold, the local electric mechanic, says customers still ask for a tank fill-up, and he reminds them "You 'charge' it, not 'fill' it."
The city council organized a fair called 'Electric Enlightenment' on October 10th, featuring test drives, info booths, and French fries.
At the fair, councilmember Susan Smith accidentally activated autonomous mode and professed her love for the vehicle as it navigated cones.
The article frames the switch as a way to cut the local carbon footprint, improve air quality, and say goodbye to the pricey gas pump.
Taxi drivers view autonomous cars with suspicion, fearing unemployment; cabby Tony 'Tires' McLire jokes they will take over the pizzeria.
The piece concludes that EVs and autonomous cars promise a cleaner, more efficient future, while also producing comic moments as residents talk to their cars.
